notes: This is one half of Openstaande posten's mapping, not the whole module: the template's 'Debiteur of Crediteur' column (D/C, required, index 0) decides which of two field-shapes a row actually goes through — both go through the same connector (`FiEntries`, unlike the Debiteuren/Crediteuren split, which is two different connectors), but 'Kenmerk rekening' (`VaAs`) and which amount field gets filled (`AmDe` vs `AmCr`) differ by side. This file covers 'D' rows; 'C' rows go through the sibling file erp-openstaandposten-crediteur.json instead. Same shape of seam as `erp-debiteuren-organisatie.json`/`-persoon.json`, and the same limitation applies: `module` here is the shared app module id (`erp-openstaandposten`), not a unique key, so `_module_connector()` in main.py would resolve 'the mapping for erp-openstaandposten' to whichever of these two files sorts first if anything ever reads it that way — see docs/todo.md.

Not mapped at all: the 'Debiteur of Crediteur' switch column itself. It has no AFAS field of its own — it only decides which of these two files a row's other columns feed — so it is consumed by the branching logic above, never by a field mapping.

REPLACES the previous single-file mapping (pre-18-08-2026), which was written against `ERP 6_Openstaande posten.xlsx` — two sheets ('Debiteuren Openstaand' / 'Crediteuren Openstaand') sharing one column layout, with the debiteur/crediteur distinction implicit in which sheet a row was read from. The redesigned template (`ERP_9_Openstaande posten.xlsx`) collapsed that into one sheet with this explicit D/C column instead, which is what makes `VaAs` (previously unmapped — no column could supply it) mappable at all: it is fixed per file rather than needing to vary per row within one file.
VaAs (Kenmerk rekening) is fixed '2' (Debiteur) for this file's rows — every row here comes through the 'D' branch, so every row is a debiteur-side account line.

AmDe (Bedrag debet) carries the template's `Bedrag` column (named `Debet` until 13-10-2026, when it was renamed because it carries crediteur amounts too); AmCr is a fixed 0 on this line and receives the amount on the counter-line.

BALANCED by a counter-line (Taroen, 13-10-2026). The referentie (§6.4) states a journaalpost must be in balans, AmDe-totaal = AmCr-totaal, and a beginbalans of only debiteuren is all-debet. So every row is written as **two** regels: its own line, and a counter-line on the row's `Tussenrekening` column — `VaAs` 1 (Grootboekrekening), `AcNr` the tussenrekening, `AmDe`/`AmCr` swapped, `AuPa`/`InId`/`DaEx` left out (they belong to a debiteur/crediteur line). Each boekstuk therefore balances on its own, and with it the whole post. The counter-line is not a mapping entry: it is the plan's `counterLine` in `MODULE_PAYLOAD_PLANS` (frontend/src/lib/module-payloads.ts). `AmCr` is mapped as a fixed 0 so the opposite amount field is in the body for the swap to fill — AFAS's own FiEntries example (§6.4) sends the zero side explicitly as well.

GROUPED, same design as before the template redesign. `FiEntryPar` is a journaalpost and `FiEntries` are its boekingsregels — the same kop/regel shape as erp-voorcalculatie, and the referentie's own FiEntries example (§6.4) shows exactly this: one FiEntryPar with an ARRAY of FiEntries under it. The key is `Fin Administratie` + `Dagboek` (the two kop columns), so all of one administratie's open debiteuren-posts in one dagboek become one journaalpost with one regel each. Boekstuknummer is deliberately NOT part of the key: the rules give it a `unique` check, so keying on it would put every row back in its own post and undo the grouping.

BpNr (Boekstuknummer) and AuPa (Incasseren) are both treated as mandatory here even though AFAS's own schema marks `BpNr` optional and `AuPa` optional too — the template's own rules make both `required`, and per policy the template's rule wins. `AuPa` is also a judgment call: the closest boolean AFAS field to 'collect this via direct debit' for 'Incasseren', type-matching the sheet's J/N values, but not a literal label match — worth confirming.

Dates and period (Taroen, 13-10-2026): `BpDa` (Boekstukdatum) comes from the template's new `Factuurdatum` column, so AFAS ages each post from its real invoice date; a blank cell falls back to the livegangdatum. `EnDa` (Datum boeking) is always the livegangdatum, and `Year`/`Peri` (Boekjaar/Periode) are that date's year and month — this assumes monthly periods. The fallback and the three derived fields are `derive` overrides in `MODULE_OVERRIDES` (frontend/src/lib/module-phases.ts), not mapping entries; a project without a livegangdatum omits them and AFAS refuses the post on the mandatory fields. Left unmapped: `EnNo` (Nummer journaalpost, this line's own primary key, mandatory) — **confirmed AFAS-assigned on create (08-09-2026)**, so not a gap and not blocking. Two POSTs of the same balanced post to `connectors/FiEntries` in a test environment, both with `EnNo` omitted entirely, each answered 201 with the number AFAS had picked in the response body: `results.FiEntryPar.EnNo` = 77820, then 77821. A supplied primary-key volgnummer *is* validated against existing keys on this connector family (the sibling `HrMobility#CcSn` answers 'The primary key already exists for field Volgnummer' for a taken value), so an auto-incrementing 201 on an omitted `EnNo` is positive proof AFAS assigns it rather than silently defaulting to 0. Same category as `HrCompMut#Id` (hrm-vakantietoeslag.json): metainfo flags it mandatory because that applies to an update, and a conversion only ever POSTs. Correctly left unmapped — sending it would fight AFAS's own counter. The AFAS reference's own FiEntries example (§6.4) likewise omits it. The remaining ~30 optional fields on FiEntries (Btw-code, currency/koers fields, payment terms, project/campagne references, FiDimEntries/FiPrjEntries/FiTransEntries, etc.) have no column and aren't required — left out entirely rather than listed one by one.

verifiedAgainst.description: Live GET /api/afas/updateconnectors/modules/FiEntries — unchanged since the 13-08-2026 check: 8 top-level fields, one nested object 'FiEntries' (43 fields, VaAs values 1=Grootboekrekening/2=Debiteur/3=Crediteur), which itself nests FiDimEntries/FiPrjEntries/FiTransEntries (not used by this mapping). Root/name is 'FiEntryPar', not 'FiEntries'. Only the Excel template changed on 18-08-2026, not the connector.
